why: The student finds and fixes the bug in this one failing case: the cast applies to Math.random() before the multiply, so the die is always 1 and never 6, which is why the result is 0.0. Fixing one given failing case is L3, not L4.

concepts.quote: The cast happens first, so (int) Math.random() is 0 and the die is always 1. Cast after multiplying.
concepts.why: Correctly links when the cast happens to the range of Math.random(): casting first gives 0, so the cast has to cover the whole product.

concepts.quote: (int) Math.random() is 0 and the die is always 1
concepts.why: Uses the fact that Math.random() returns a value in [0,1) to explain why casting first always gives 0, then fixes the code by casting after multiplying.
The answer makes no claim about the random move.
